name: Yale Institute for Global Health

tagline.text: Hub for Global Health at Yale

subtagline: One institute. Many schools. Shared impact.
intro: YIGH is Yale’s focal point for global health. Rooted in the Schools of Medicine, Nursing, and Public Health, the Institute connects interdisciplinary expertise across the university to address global health challenges.
history: Approved by the Yale Corporation and launched in 2019, YIGH was anchored in Medicine, Nursing, and Public Health with a university-wide mandate to convene faculty, students, and partners and translate Yale’s scholarship into greater global impact.

mission.text: To serve as the interdisciplinary hub for global health at Yale by cultivating scholarship, leadership, and innovation through research and education with partners to advance health worldwide.

vision: A world where institutions engage in equitable partnerships with shared resolve to address global health challenges.

values.name: One Yale
values.text: We harness the full breadth of Yale by connecting disciplines, schools, and perspectives, breaking down silos and creating opportunities for collaboration that no single part of the university could achieve alone.

values.name: Reciprocal Partnerships
values.text: We build equitable partnerships grounded in mutual respect, co-design, shared priorities, and bi-directional exchange, ensuring that collaboration creates meaningful and lasting value for all partners.

values.name: Collective Engagement
values.text: We bring together academic, practitioner, community, and policy perspectives to co-create solutions, translate evidence into action, and elevate voices and ideas that can improve health and influence policy and practice.

values.name: Principled Excellence
values.text: We pursue excellence in everything we do, upholding high ethical standards and demonstrating transparency, accountability, rigor, and integrity in our work and commitments.

values.name: Enduring Impact
values.text: We steward YIGH's resources, relationships, and opportunities responsibly, prioritizing investments that maximize impact while building durable programs, partnerships, and capacity for the future.

approach.intro: YIGH connects Yale’s people, ideas, resources, and partners, turning the university’s breadth of expertise into collective global health impact.

items.name: Convene & Catalyze
items.text: We bring faculty, students, practitioners, and partners together across disciplines to spark new ideas, seed collaborations, and catalyze collective action on complex global health challenges.

items.name: Administer & Operate
items.text: We provide the infrastructure, funding, and operational support that enable global health ideas and programs to thrive, from experiential learning and fellowships to grants and growing university-wide initiatives.

items.name: Collaborate & Connect
items.text: We serve as a connector within Yale and a point of entry for external partners, linking people, expertise, resources, and opportunities across schools, disciplines, sectors, and geographies to build stronger interdisciplinary collaborations.

items.name: Recognize & Amplify
items.text: We elevate Yale’s global health expertise, research, and impact, giving greater visibility to faculty, students, partners, and communities while translating knowledge into awareness, policy, and action.

priorities_intro: YIGH’s four strategic priorities focus the Institute’s interdisciplinary strengths on areas where global health needs are rapidly evolving and where Yale can bring distinctive expertise to bear.

priorities.name: Climate & Health
priorities.summary: Build climate-resilient health systems by connecting Yale’s strengths in planetary science, public health, data, policy, and social science with partners addressing climate-related health risks.
priorities.text: The Institute will help build climate-resilient health systems by connecting Yale’s strengths in planetary science, public health, data, policy, and social science with partners addressing climate-related health risks around the world. The Institute will support interdisciplinary approaches that anticipate emerging threats, translate evidence into practical tools and policy, strengthen decision-making capacity, and co-design locally relevant approaches to resilience and adaptation.

priorities.name: Digital Health & AI
priorities.summary: Harness AI, data science, and digital health to strengthen diagnostics, surveillance, care delivery, and health-system decision-making.
priorities.text: The Institute will harness advances in artificial intelligence, data science, and digital health to strengthen diagnostics, surveillance, care delivery, and health-system decision-making. Working across Yale and with global partners, the Institute will help move promising technologies from innovation to responsible implementation, supporting evidence generation, governance and regulatory capacity, workforce readiness, and equitable adoption, particularly in resource-constrained settings.

priorities.name: Health Diplomacy & Security
priorities.summary: Connect Yale’s academic expertise with global policy, preparedness, and multilateral action on health challenges that cross borders.
priorities.text: The Institute will connect Yale’s academic expertise with global policy, preparedness, and multilateral action to address health challenges that cross borders and require collective solutions. Through partnerships with governments, regional and multilateral institutions, and other global actors, YIGH will help translate research into policy, strengthen preparedness and response capacity, and cultivate leaders equipped to navigate the increasingly complex intersection of health, diplomacy, and security.

priorities.name: Health Sovereignty
priorities.summary: Advance a country-led approach to global health, supporting the institutions, capabilities, and partnerships countries need to define and deliver their own health priorities.
priorities.text: The Institute will advance a more country-led approach to global health by supporting the institutions, capabilities, and partnerships countries need to define and deliver their own health priorities. This includes strengthening pathways from biomedical discovery to equitable access, building local research and implementation capacity, and supporting sustainable approaches to health financing, regulation, manufacturing, and health-system delivery, shifting the emphasis from dependency toward ownership, resilience, and lasting institutional capacity.

pillars_intro: Four institutional pillars cut across the strategic priorities: the enduring ways YIGH builds and strengthens people, ideas and solutions, knowledge and evidence, and relationships and capacity.

pillars.name: Partners
pillars.text: Trusted, reciprocal partnerships that strengthen institutions, communities, and health systems, connecting Yale’s expertise with locally defined priorities.

pillars.name: Leaders
pillars.text: Opportunities for students, trainees, faculty, and practitioners to build the knowledge, experience, networks, and skills needed to lead in a changing global health landscape.

pillars.name: Innovators
pillars.text: Bold ideas and transformative solutions, supported by catalytic funding and pathways that move ideas from concept to real-world application and impact.

pillars.name: Scholars
pillars.text: Interdisciplinary team science, emerging investigators, global research collaborations, and bidirectional exchange that translate evidence into policy, practice, and improved health.
